title: Chapter 85 — The Follow-Up System: Architecture of the Second Yes
intro: The pipeline pools operationalised and the sequence library.

sections.title: Most Sales Die of Silence
sections.content:
Most appliance quotes die of silence, not rejection. The data says it takes 3-5 touches to close a quote that walked out. Most salespeople follow up once and quit.

The follow-up system is not optional. It is the architecture that turns a 15 percent walk-out conversion rate into a 35 percent conversion rate. That difference alone can add $50,000 to your annual income.

sections.title: The Sequence
sections.content:
Day 0 — same-day thank-you text within 2 hours. Day 1 — formal quote email with images and specs. Day 3 — phone call, not text. Day 7 — value-add: comparison chart, review article, installation video. Day 14 — honest check-in with promo deadline reminder. Day 30 — long-game touch.

Every touch must add information the customer did not have. Never 'just checking in.' That phrase communicates zero value.

sections.title: The CRM Is the System
sections.content:
Log every touch. Tag the reason for no-close. Set the next follow-up date before you hang up or send.

The patterns in your CRM tell you where your floor process is breaking. If 80 percent of your stalled quotes are price objections, your value presentation needs work. If 60 percent are spouse delays, your kitchen-table kit needs upgrading. The data coaches you if you let it.
